steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Food labels are legally required to provide: name of the food, ingredients list (in descending order of weight), allergen information, net quantity, use-by or best-before date, storage instructions, and name/address of the manufacturer.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The traffic light labelling system uses colour coding: green (low — healthier choice), amber (moderate), red (high — eat in smaller amounts or less often) for fat, saturated fat, sugars, and salt.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Use-by dates are about safety: food should NOT be eaten after its use-by date, even if it looks and smells fine (particularly for high-risk foods like meat and dairy).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Best-before dates are about quality: food is at its best before this date but is usually still safe to eat afterwards (e.g. dried pasta, tinned goods).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between a use-by date and a best-before date? | Q: What do the three colours in the traffic light labelling system mean? | Q: List four of the 14 major allergens that must be declared on food labels.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A use-by date is about safety — food should not be eaten after this date. A best-before date is about quality — food may still be safe to eat after this date but may not be at its best. | Green = low (healthier choice), amber = moderate, red = high (eat less often or in smaller amounts). They apply to fat, saturated fat, sugars, and salt. | Celery, cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, lupin, milk, molluscs, mustard, nuts, peanuts, sesame, soybeans, sulphur dioxide (any four).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the difference between use-by and best-before — this is a very common exam question. When asked about traffic light labels, state what each colour means AND which nutrients are colour-coded (fat, saturated fat, sugars, salt). Be ready to list at least 4 of the 14 allergens — examiners do not usually require all 14. When discussing marketing, always explain HOW a technique influences consumer behaviour, not just what it is.
